item.title: Wave Hill: 2027 Sunroom Project Space (NYC)
item.description:
Organisation: Wave Hill

Location: Glyndor Gallery, Wave Hill, the Bronx, New York City, USA. For early-career artists living within a 50-mile radius of the Bronx.

Award: $2,000 honorarium per artist, plus exhibition and professional development support, a co-designed Meet the Artist public program, and a short exhibition essay published in print and online. Four artists selected. No application fee.

Duration: Nine to twelve months of research and development leading to a solo presentation during the 2027 season

Deadline: Closed 09 Aug 2026

The Sunroom Project Space gives artists in the New York City area who are in the early stages of their careers, regardless of age, the chance to develop and show a site-specific solo project in the Sunroom or Sun Porch of Glyndor Gallery at Wave Hill. For the 2027 season, Wave Hill is especially interested in projects that recognise ancestral wisdom in relation to our connection with the earth and soil: practices, beliefs and values passed down through generations, particularly those that foster harmonious relationships with our ecosystems, for example regenerative farming and agricultural practices and the care of soil, water and plant life. Projects engaging the history of earth or land art (concepts, materials, sites and relationships to place) that intersect with sustainable practices and ancestral wisdom are also welcome. AWARD: four artists are selected for solo presentations, each receiving a $2,000 honorarium, exhibition and professional development support, and nine to twelve months to research and develop their ideas. Each project is accompanied by a Meet the Artist program co-designed with the artist, and a short exhibition essay published in print and online. ELIGIBILITY: artists working across media, in the early stages of their career regardless of education, living within a 50-mile radius of the Bronx. Not eligible: students enrolled in a degree-granting program; artists with commercial gallery representation; artists who have previously exhibited a site-specific project at Wave Hill; artists who participated in the 2026 Winter Workspace program at Wave Hill. Applications are reviewed by a jury of Wave Hill's Curator of Visual Arts, an invited guest curator and a prior 2026 Sunroom Project Space artist. An online information session is held Monday 13 July, 12-1PM; RSVP to visualarts@wavehill.org with the subject line '2027 Sunroom Project Space Info Session'. DEADLINE: 9 August 2026. Apply via SlideRoom.

item.title: Queens Museum: QM-Jerome Foundation Fellowship for Emerging Artists 2027-2028
item.description:
Organisation: Queens Museum (with the Jerome Foundation)

Location: Queens, New York City, USA

Award: $20,000 fellowship award per artist (two artists selected), plus professional development consultations, mentorship from Queens Museum staff and an established New York-based artist, and a solo exhibition at the Queens Museum in 2028. No application fee.

Duration: One-year fellowship (2027-2028), culminating in a 2028 solo exhibition

Deadline: 28 Sep 2026

The QM-Jerome Foundation Fellowship for Emerging Artists selects two emerging visual artists living in New York City for its 2027-2028 cohort. Each fellow receives a $20,000 award, professional development consultations, mentorship from Queens Museum staff and an established New York-based artist, and a solo exhibition at the Queens Museum in 2028, with curatorial support across a full year of project development. Aimed at early-career visual artists (roughly two to ten years of professional practice) who have a consistent practice and developing public profile but have not yet reached major institutional recognition. ELIGIBILITY: must currently reside in one of NYC's five boroughs and maintain residency through the fellowship; artists enrolled in degree-granting programs are not eligible; review the detailed criteria on exhibition history, previous grants and years of practice. Supported by the Jerome Foundation. Apply via the Queens Museum fellowship program page. Deadline: 28 September 2026, 11:59 PM EST.

item.title: City of Moorhead: 2026 Call for Public Art (Movable Interactive Piece)
item.description:
Organisation: City of Moorhead, Minnesota

Location: Moorhead, Minnesota, USA. The piece will be sited at different locations throughout the city. No geographic eligibility restriction is stated in the call, so non-US artists appear eligible, but this is not confirmed in writing.

Award: Not published. The call announcement states no budget, commission amount or artist fee, and the linked Request for Art document could not be retrieved. Confirm the budget with art@moorheadmn.gov before investing time in a proposal. No application fee is mentioned.

Duration: Single commission; timeline not published

Deadline: 04 Sep 2026

The City of Moorhead is seeking proposals for an inspirational, movable public artwork to be installed at rotating locations across the city. Interactive elements are explicitly encouraged, with kinetic sculpture, digital installation and tactile elements named as examples. Strong proposals invite public participation, promote creativity and youth engagement, are safe for all members of the public, are durable enough for year-round outdoor conditions, and draw people to gather. Submissions are reviewed and ranked by the Artist Review Team, whose recommendation passes to the Art and Culture Commission and then to City Council for the final decision. Questions go to art@moorheadmn.gov. Proposals are due by 10:00am on Friday 4 September 2026.

Open call details

item.title: The Gallery at Penn College: 2027-28 Call for Exhibitions
item.description:
Organisation: The Gallery at Penn College (Pennsylvania College of Technology)

Location: Williamsport, Pennsylvania, USA, on the Pennsylvania College of Technology campus. Travel note: Williamsport Regional Airport connects only to Washington Dulles, with no other direct flights or trains, so international travel involves a connection. No nationality restriction is stated.

Award: Housing, meals, a solo exhibition honorarium, and a shipping and travel stipend are all provided. Specific figures are not published in the call. No application fee is stated.

Duration: Exhibition slot within the 2027-28 season; review takes place during autumn semester with artists notified in January

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

The Gallery at Penn College is accepting proposals for solo, two-person and group exhibitions in its 2027-28 season. All entries are juried through a blind selection process by a gallery committee of faculty, staff, K-12 art educators and community artists. The space is 3,000 square feet with 82 to 250 running feet of linear wall depending on configuration and a ceiling height of 11 feet 4 inches, and all exhibitions are installed by gallery staff. Site-specific installations requiring artist installation need an approved planning document first. Campus visits are a valued part of programming though some exhibitions are scheduled without one; visiting artists give a 20 to 30 minute gallery talk at the public reception, and are encouraged to propose class-specific programmes or community workshops. Promotional support includes an annual gallery catalogue, postcards, press releases and web and social coverage. Applications require 10 to 15 digital images (JPG only, max 4 MB each), an image list with dimensions and medium, a CV and an artist statement.

Open call details

item.title: Cafe Royal Cultural Foundation: Performance Grant (Summer 2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Cafe Royal Cultural Foundation NYC

Location: New York City (five boroughs), or a location in close proximity to NYC approved by the foundation, USA

Award: Up to $10,000 for production costs (performers, collaborators, rehearsal and venue rental, design elements, technical staff, etc.). Does not fund the creation or composition of new work. No application fee.

Duration: Production grant; performance must start no sooner than 1 November 2026 and complete by 22 September 2027

Deadline: Closed 03 Aug 2026

The Cafe Royal Cultural Foundation NYC Performance Grant supports individual artists producing theatre, dance and performance art (which may be accompanied by music) moving toward a public performance. The Summer 2026 cycle offers up to $10,000 for eligible production costs: actors, dancers and guest performers, director/choreographer/composer and creative-team fees, costumes, lighting, sound, scenic, props and set, rehearsal and venue rental, and production and technical staff. Funds do not cover the creation or composition of new work; if the performance is a play it must be a full production (readings do not qualify). ELIGIBILITY: individual performers only (not groups or organizations) who are US citizens or resident aliens, current NYC residents who have lived in the city at least one year and will remain through project completion. This cycle accepts only 40 applications and closes early if that cap is reached. Applicants may submit up to 5 video links. Apply via the foundation's performance page. Deadline: 3 August 2026, 9:00 am ET (or earlier if 40 applications are received).

item.title: Adrianna Newell Fellowship at Arts&Rec 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Arts&Rec Inc

Location: Stamford, NY (Western Catskills), USA

Award: Live/work residency: use of a 1000 sq ft studio and attached apartment, plus a $1,500 total materials stipend and per diem. Travel (especially international) is not funded. No application fee.

Duration: October 2026 (four weeks to two months, based on project needs; possible extension into November)

Deadline: Closed 31 Jul 2026

Inaugural Adrianna Newell Fellowship, a live/work studio residency in Stamford, NY (Western Catskills) for October 2026, with possible extension into November. Named for board member Adrianna Newell, it invites queer lens-based artists working in photography and moving image with an active, research-driven or conceptually rich practice, especially work engaging queer perspectives on land, rurality and regional space, or queer identity, memory, intimacy, community and embodiment. Open to artists from everywhere. Fellows receive a 1000 sq ft studio with attached apartment, a $1,500 combined materials stipend and per diem, and introductions to the local creative community; an open-studio presentation, artist talk or public exhibition at the end is required. Travel, especially international, is not funded (residents are encouraged to seek travel support elsewhere). Apply by emailing a single PDF (one-page description of your work and planned project, 10 to 20 work samples with short descriptions, and a current CV) to programs@artsrec.org. Deadline: 31 July 2026; notices by end of August.

Open call details

item.title: James Castle House: 2027 Artist Residencies (Boise, Idaho)
item.description:
Organisation: James Castle House / City of Boise

Location: Boise, Idaho, USA. Open to applicants legally able to work in the United States.

Award: $4,000 stipend for two-month terms or $1,000 for two-week terms, to assist with living expenses and supplies, plus solo live-in accommodation and studio at the historic James Castle House. Residents donate one selected piece to the City of Boise collection at the end of the term. No application fee.

Duration: Two-month terms (1 Mar - 30 Apr, 1 Jun - 31 Jul, 1 Sep - 31 Oct 2027) or two-week terms (11-25 Jan and 1-15 Dec 2027)

Deadline: 28 Aug 2026

The James Castle House in Boise, Idaho (the preserved home of self-taught artist James Castle) opens applications for its 2027 residency terms from 16 July to 28 August 2026. TWO-MONTH RESIDENCY: an immersive focus on a project or body of work responding to the history and legacy of James Castle or the site; open to artists, scholars, creators and professionals in any field; $4,000 stipend; residents share their practice through public events (workshops, open studios, presentations) and donate a selected piece to the City of Boise collection. Terms: 1 March - 30 April, 1 June - 31 July, or 1 September - 31 October 2027. TWO-WEEK RESIDENCY: time and space for a single site-responsive project; $1,000 stipend; one public event. Terms: 11-25 January or 1-15 December 2027. A rolling PROJECT RESIDENCY also considers proposals case by case (email jamescastlehouse@cityofboise.org). ELIGIBILITY: 18+, legally able to work in the United States, able to pass a background check; emerging and mid-career practitioners in any field, though the property cannot accommodate loud or especially messy processes. Residents live alone on site. Selection by committee on strength of proposal, application, work samples and references. Virtual information session 21 July 2026, 1pm MT. Applicants notified September 2026. DEADLINE: 28 August 2026.

Open call details

item.title: Wave Hill / AnkhLave Arts Alliance: 2027 Van Lier Fellowship (NYC)
item.description:
Organisation: Wave Hill / AnkhLave Arts Alliance

Location: Wave Hill Public Garden and Cultural Center, the Bronx, New York City, USA. For NYC-based BIPOC visual artists aged 30 or younger.

Award: $10,435 stipend, including an $8,000 honorarium, a transportation stipend for the residency, and professional development opportunities, plus the Winter Workspace residency, a solo exhibition with public programs, mentorship from Wave Hill curatorial staff and arts professionals, and AnkhLave Alumni Network benefits. Two fellowships awarded. No application fee.

Duration: January to December 2027; Winter Workspace residency 23 February - 18 April 2027; solo exhibition 15 May - 4 July 2027

Deadline: Closed 10 Aug 2026

Wave Hill, in partnership with AnkhLave Arts Alliance, invites NYC-based artists who identify as BIPOC to apply for the 2027 Van Lier Fellowship as part of the 9th Annual AnkhLave Garden Project at Wave Hill Public Garden and Cultural Center in the Bronx. The project supports artists who draw on research, scholarship and lived knowledge to present site-responsive work at the intersection of nature, culture and place, engaging with Wave Hill's plant collections, history, design and architecture. The Van Lier Fellowship (funded by the Edward and Sally Van Lier Fund through the New York Community Trust) will be awarded to two NYC-based visual artists aged 30 or younger. FELLOWSHIP: participation in the Winter Workspace residency (23 February - 18 April 2027); a $10,435 stipend including an $8,000 honorarium and transportation stipend; a solo exhibition in the Sunroom or Sun Porch (15 May - 4 July 2027); public engagement through Winter Workspace programming and a Meet the Artist program; mentorship with Wave Hill curatorial staff, working artists and arts professionals; and AnkhLave Alumni Network benefits. ELIGIBILITY: emerging artists 30 or younger (born 1997 or after) from historically underrepresented communities; live in one of the five NYC boroughs; demonstrate financial need; have completed college and not be enrolled in a degree-granting program during the residency; not represented by a commercial gallery; available for both programs; cannot have been a Van Lier Fellow elsewhere or have previously done a Winter Workspace residency or exhibited at Wave Hill or with AnkhLave. Works may not include nudity, depictions of violence or profanity. Artists may apply to only one of the two 2027 AnkhLave Garden Project opportunities. Questions: visualarts@wavehill.org with '2027 Van Lier-Ankhlave' in the subject. DEADLINE: 10 August 2026. Apply via SlideRoom.

Open call details

item.title: JCAL: ARTWorks Fellowship 2026-2027
item.description:
Organisation: Jamaica Center for Arts and Learning (JCAL)

Location: Jamaica, Queens, New York City, USA. Open to visual artists based in New York City (preferably Queens) or Long Island; priority to Queens-based BIIPOC artists.

Award: $5,000 per Fellow, paid out over the course of the program, plus free shared studio space at JCAL (about 550 sq ft, as available), a 7 x 4 ft storage closet, one free JCAL class (space-available), an Artist Mentor and seminar series, and a concluding two-month group exhibition with catalogue in JCAL's Miller and Community galleries. No application fee.

Duration: Six-month fellowship: 7 October 2026 to 18 June 2027; exhibition opens 9 April 2027

Deadline: Closed 13 Jul 2026

Jamaica Center for Arts and Learning (JCAL) invites New York City-based visual artists to apply for ARTWorks, its Artist Fellowship Training Seminar Series: a six-month fellowship focused on career sustainability that amplifies the work of emerging, underrepresented visual artists. Six Fellows treat their practice as a small business, set entrepreneurial and professional goals, and build a long-term plan, supported by a Program Manager, an established Artist Mentor, cohort meetings, and at least six seminar events (past topics: copyright and contracts, working with galleries and collectors, grant writing, taxes and accounting, marketing, art handling). SUPPORT: $5,000 per Fellow paid over the program, free shared studio space (about 550 sq ft, as available) with a storage closet, one free JCAL class, and a concluding two-month group exhibition with catalogue (opens 9 April 2027). ELIGIBILITY: reside in New York City (preferably Queens) or Long Island; identify as BIIPOC (Black, Immigrant, Indigenous, People of Color); demonstrate clarity of concept and strong craft with a deep commitment to social practice; must NOT have received major exposure via exhibitions, grants or residencies; must not be enrolled in any college degree or certificate program; past Fellows ineligible. Priority to Queens-based artists of underrepresented communities; multidisciplinary practices welcome, but the program focuses on visual artists working in traditional forms. APPLY via Submittable with six images OR two 3-5 minute videos, a one-page work-sample description, artist statement (max 300 words), one professional reference (max 300 words), CV, and a paragraph on your expectations of ARTWorks. Jury reviews submissions without obvious identifiers. TIMELINE: first-round notifications 3 August 2026, interviews 11-14 August, Fellows notified 21 August, program runs 7 October 2026 to 18 June 2027. DEADLINE: midnight Monday 13 July 2026 (portal closes 14 July 2026, 6:00 AM ET).

Open call details
